html:
SMTO-LLM-0088 — Your model account has run out of credit

GUID: fb02056f-a938-4e01-b0d1-102d2998132e
Slug: provider-quota-exhausted
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: readiness

What happened

  • The model service says this account has used up its allowance, such as its credits or spending limit. Waiting a few minutes won't fix it; more allowance has to be added.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the person who manages the model service account to check its billing, credits and spending limits, and add more allowance. The service won't accept more requests from this account until it has allowance again.
  2. Or, on the Main card in Settings › Setup › Model routing, enter an API key for an account that has credit, and select Save Main. A different account with allowance can serve requests right away.
  3. Select Check saved model. When it passes, select Resume on the stopped task. This confirms the account works again before your task continues, and finished work is kept.

What success looks like

  • Check saved model reports passed, and the task continues.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the model service account. Don't raise SMTO's time limits or keep retrying; the account needs more allowance first.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The model provider returned HTTP 429 with error code insufficient_quota, meaning the account's billing, credit or spending limit is exhausted rather than a short-term rate limit.

What this means

  • The provider identified an account allowance restriction. Waiting for a short rate-limit interval or increasing SMTO timeouts will not establish that billing or spending limits have recovered.

Why this can happen

  • The provider identified an account allowance restriction. Waiting for a short rate-limit interval or increasing SMTO timeouts will not establish that billing or spending limits have recovered.

How to diagnose it

  • The provider returned HTTP 429 with an explicit insufficient_quota code.
  • The provider accepts a bounded model request under the intended account.

How to fix it

  • Have the account administrator check billing status, prepaid credits and project or organization spending limits in the provider console, and restore allowance. Waiting out a rate-limit window or increasing SMTO timeouts will not help; confirm with Check saved model before submitting work again.
  • Ask the account administrator to check billing, credits and project spending limits. Restore an allowance before submitting work again.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded condition before trying the affected request again. Inspect existing operation receipts before resuming saved work.

How to verify the fix

  • The provider accepts a bounded model request under the intended account.

What not to do

  • Do not replay completed work or weaken authentication and certificate checks to clear this diagnostic.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic describes the observed failure; it does not establish the outcome of earlier operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
